page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-8GB is an entry-tier virtual server running on KVM hypervisor architecture. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 4 physical cores clocked at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 8 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 40 GB local SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluation reveals exceptionally strong single-threaded performance alongside moderate multi-threaded throughput. Single-core stress-ng scores rank in the top 10 percent, mirrored by a Geekbench single-core score of 2316.0 and superior single-threaded compression throughput in gzip and bzip3. However, overall multi-core capacity registers in the middle tier, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 6779.0 and multi-core stress-ng achieving average results. In memory testing, cached read operations operate at 850.79 GB/s, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure 90.32 GB/s and 56.62 GB/s respectively, with PassMark memory evaluation rating in the lower quartile.

The 1:2 RAM ratio and shared-allocation vCPUs present specific performance tradeoffs. Small model text generation performs well with 300.47 tokens per second on a 135M model, but larger 7B model prompt processing falls into the bottom 25 percent. The system is well configured for development environments, web serving, CI/CD runners, lightweight text processing, and auxiliary task workers where strong single-core clock response outweighs large memory footprint requirements.
description: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 4 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 8 GB of RAM, and 40 GB of local SSD storage, this instance delivers a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets. Benchmark assessments highlight top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong single-threaded compression performance, complemented by average multi-core metrics and moderate memory bandwidth. Due to its balanced shared-core resource profile and compact storage allocation, the instance provides cost-efficient compute capacity best suited for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, batch data compression, and standard application development workloads.
